- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion zones — if price is 3–5% below 30-day moving average, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model exhibits lag — forecast should be adjusted to align with 2–3 day sentiment trend, not 1-day sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — if true outcome shows strong upward trend in last 5 days, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for final 5 days.
